records.name: Exceed Marketing Solutions
keyPersonnel: David P. Bolthouse (founder and CEO; manager in Florida's corporate register)
Barbro M. Bolthouse (manager in Florida's corporate register)
otherServices: Manages clients' "ancillary sites, social media, directory listings, hosting and email accounts"
"Search Ranking and AI Inclusion (SEO and GEO)"
records.notes: Describes itself as "a leading marketing partner for boarding schools and adolescent therapeutic programs, helping them achieve and maintain full enrollment," and tells programs that "participation with Exceed includes free featured listings in our highly ranked directories." Its directories tell parents their owners have "no ownership, investment, equity interest, or controlling interest in any program featured or listed." On October 2, 2026, 15 of the 16 program and directory websites that publish instructions for AI chatbots (llms.txt) were made with Exceed's software; the programs listed above are the ones whose websites were. A former director of Brush Creek Academy and New Lifehouse Academy gives a testimonial on Exceed's site. Exceed's website, the Best Choice Admissions sites and Exceed's directories share one Bing webmaster verification code.

records.name: Best Choice Admissions Services
keyPersonnel: David Bolthouse (chief executive, as The Warren reported in 2022)
otherServices: The help line on Exceed Marketing Solutions' directories; TeenChallengeSchools.com labels its pages "by Best Choice Admissions"
records.notes: Its home page says that "BEST CHOICE IS SPONSORED BY SCHOOLS AND PROGRAMS, THEREFORE OUR HELP IS OFFERED AT NO CHARGE TO FAMILIES." It shares a Spanish-language phone number with the Exceed directories. Earlier it told parents it was "a contracted agent of institutions" paid "a flat fee" for every enrollment; today it says it does not favor programs "based on financial incentives."

records.name: The Envoy Group
keyPersonnel: David Bolthouse (founder, as The Warren reported)
otherServices: A referral network: programs passed on parents' inquiries that were "not a good fit for your program (usually 90% or more aren't)" to other network programs
records.notes: Its pitch to programs: "easily referring inquiries that are not a good fit for your program (usually 90% or more aren't) with other network programs, and offset marketing costs while doing so," and "We custom target leads based on what parents are already searching for." Its site now says it "has closed its doors."

records.name: All Kinds of Therapy
keyPersonnel: Jenney Wilder (founder; closed her educational consulting practice in 2015)
otherServices: Directory listings for programs at $400 a month
records.notes: Its listing pages say "No pay-to-rank listings. Everyone here is human-verified." A 2026 press release calls it "a leading consumer-advocacy platform." Its listing for Provo Canyon School still called it "a leading national provider of residential youth treatment" after Utah ordered the school's last campus closed in July 2026.
